LESSON: INDIGENOUS KENYAN GAMES (OPTIONAL)

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Dislaying
Topic 2.5: Indigenous Kenyan games (optional)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Indigenous Kenyan games (optional), part of Performing and Dislaying in Grade 6 CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How do floor games enhance physical fitness? 2. Why are floor games considered as indigenous?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch a virtual or live demonstration of indigenous floor game and identify the skills observed,

2. demonstrate indigenous floor games while observing safety,

3. practise indigenous floor games while observing safety,

4. practise different types of indigenous floor games while combining it to a musical rhythm.

5. talk about the role of indigenous floor games in enhancing fitness with peers. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch a virtual or live demonstration of indigenous floor game and identify the skills observed,
2. demonstrate indigenous floor games while observing safety,
3. practise indigenous floor games while observing safety,
4. practise different types of indigenous floor games while combining it to a musical rhythm.
5. talk about the role of indigenous floor games in enhancing fitness with peers. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Indigenous Kenyan games (optional) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner takes on different roles in indigenous floor games.

• Unity: The learner works with others in indigenous floor games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: The learner observes safety rules when playing indigenous floor games.

• Health and Fitness: The learner improves fitness through practicing indigenous floor games for a healthy lifestyle.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: The learner keeps counting during practise of indigenous floor games.
